completion_data.completion_summary: Implemented all 5 phases: actionable NO TEXT LAYER/QUALITY GATE FAILED remedy messaging in literature-convert.sh, a distinct needs-OCR bucket in literature-ingest.sh, an explicit never-auto LITERATURE_CONVERTER=ocr mode built on ocrmypdf, a 12-test regression suite, and updated documentation. Also fixed a pre-existing gap where the mandatory fallback tier's image-block placeholder text was masking genuinely image-only PDFs from ever reaching the exit-2 path.

memory_candidates.content: When testing a bash pipeline that shells out to `command -v <tool>` for graceful-absence detection on a single-bin-dir Linux distro (e.g. NixOS, where bash/python3/every CLI tool live in one directory like /run/current-system/sw/bin), do NOT mask the tool by overriding PATH to exclude that whole directory -- it breaks the shebang/env resolution of the test harness itself. Instead build a scratch directory of symlinks to every OTHER entry in that directory (excluding only the target tool(s)), and invoke the script under test via `bash <script>` explicitly rather than relying on its own `#!/usr/bin/env bash` shebang, so the calling shell (not the masked PATH) resolves `bash` itself.

A `LITERATURE_PYENV_DIR`-style env var pointed at a nonexistent-but-writable scratch directory does NOT reliably simulate 'primary tier unavailable' in a test, when the provisioning script (e.g. via `uv venv`) will happily auto-create a venv there given network access. Use an unwritable parent directory (mkdir + chmod 000) instead, so provisioning fails deterministically regardless of network/uv availability, then restore permissions (chmod 755) before any cleanup that needs to remove it.

When an overloaded exit code needs a stderr-marker discriminator (grep-based bucketing), a marker string without unique framing (e.g. no trailing colon) can false-match an unrelated generic log line elsewhere in the same script that merely mentions the marker phrase in explanatory prose. Require a syntactic anchor (a trailing colon after the marker token, matching its one true emission site) and document the false-positive risk inline at both the emission site and the consuming grep.
